prompt:
You are given five reference images of chibi hair that the user wants ours to look like, and then one render of OUR current hair.
REFERENCES (images 1 to 5): study how this hair is built. It is not separate round sausages. It is a few BROAD, FLAT-ISH PANELS that wrap the skull like a helmet, each panel carved with fine parallel GROOVES running root to tip, so it reads as combed strands. There is a clear PARTING on top from which the panels fall left and right and to the back. The fringe is a row of panels hanging straight down the forehead, cut BLUNT (a clean horizontal edge) or swept to one side in a big curved lock that tapers to a point. The sides fall straight in front of or behind the ears; the ears show. The back is one continuous curtain with the same grooves, ending in a clean cut line. Tails (ponytail, twin tails) are thick tapered clubs with the same grooves, tied with a small band. Boys' styles are the same panels cut short: a side part, a tousled fringe of pointed locks, a neat crop. The surface is matte with a soft broad sheen.
OUR RENDER (image 6): plump separate tubes with rounded tips. The user wants the panel-and-groove look of the references instead.

Write a new ES module for the doll's hair in the reference style.

export function buildHair(THREE, opts, kit) -> THREE.Group added to the rig's "head" pivot. The head is about 0.36 wide, 0.33 tall, 0.34 deep; its centre is 0.165 above the pivot; the face is toward +z; eyes are at 0.125 above the pivot, so the forehead is tall; ears are at the sides at eye height. Shoulders are 0.075 below the pivot and 0.085 to each side.
opts = { hairStyle, hairColor, highlight, fringe: "blunt" | "sideSwept" | "curtain" | "none" } with hairStyle one of: "bob" (to the jaw, blunt cut), "longStraight" (to the waist), "longWavy", "twinTails", "sidePonytail", "highPonytail", "bun", "shortCrop" (neat, ears clear), "sidePart" (short, parted, swept), "tousled" (short, pointed locks pointing down and forward), "curtainBangs" (medium length, parted in the middle), "pixie", "curlyMedium".
Method:
- A PANEL is a curved sheet with thickness: take a guide curve from a root on the parting or crown, over the skull and down; sweep a wide, shallow, slightly convex cross-section (0.06 to 0.14 wide, 0.012 to 0.02 thick) along it with the width following a profile (for blunt cuts the tip stays wide and ends in a flat cut face; for pointed locks it tapers), keeping the sheet's inner side on the skull scaled 1.03 and offset outward layer by layer. 20 segments across, 28 along.
- GROOVES: displace the outer surface across the width with a sum of narrow ridges (8 to 14 per panel, depth 0.0015 to 0.003, slightly irregular spacing) that run the full length, and also paint the same lines faintly into a texture used as bumpMap, so strands read at any distance. computeVertexNormals.
- Lay panels like roof tiles from the parting outward: crown panels first, then side and back panels beneath them, each overlapping its neighbours by a quarter of its width, so no scalp is visible from any angle. Add a thin hair-coloured skull cap (head scaled 1.02, above the hairline only) underneath as insurance.
- The fringe panels come last and sit on top; their lower edge is at 0.20 above the pivot (never over the eyes) unless the style has no fringe.
- Keep hair outside the head (scaled 1.02), the ears, the neck and a shoulder capsule from (-0.105, -0.07, 0) to (0.105, -0.07, 0) of radius 0.045.
- Bands for tails and buns as small torus shapes in opts.highlight.
- Material: MeshPhysicalMaterial, color opts.hairColor, roughness 0.62, sheen 0.8, sheenColor opts.highlight, clearcoat 0.05.
export function sway(group, t, amount): panels below ear level rotate 1 to 3 degrees about their roots with their own phase; tails swing a little more.
export const STYLES (the list of hairStyle values) and export const FRINGES.
Rules: a plain ES module, no imports, no globals (THREE and kit are arguments; kit.canvasTexture(width, height, (ctx, w, h) => {...}) returns a THREE.CanvasTexture). No document, window, fetch or storage. Under 1,000 lines. Return only the code in one ```js block.
